<result>I found the talk and the code behind it. The tweet (posted 2026-09-21) is a 38-minute X video: "here's how i shipped 2,500 PRs last month to production". It was meant for Cursor Compile London. Its method is written up as **pstack**, an open Cursor plugin at https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack. I couldn't get a transcript of the video. Talk details below come from third-party summaries, and implementation details come from the pstack repo.

## Sourced findings

**1. Feature map**
- **Format:** plain markdown, not generated code. `/create-verification-skill` creates `.cursor/skills/verify-<app>/features/README.md` as an index of the top 3–5 user-facing features. It links to one file per feature with four required H2 sections: sub-features, how a user reaches it, how the harness drives it, and gotchas. (create-verification-skill/SKILL.md, docs/guide/06-verify-and-ship.md)
- **Contents:** the talk summaries say it records sidebar paths, entry points, keyboard shortcuts and DOM selectors that can be driven over CDP. It exists because agents that could already launch the app still "couldn't locate UI features reliably". (youtubesummary KwOX7vJyoOk, Cmoh-yR-usA)
- **Generation:** the agent reads the codebase and walks the app to build it.
- **Upkeep:** `/maintain-verification-skill` runs as a daily cloud-agent job. Parallel agents first read the source for drift, then a live pass exercises every feature even if the source looks clean. Each mismatch is sorted as either doc drift (fix the map) or a product regression (report it). This skill never edits product code.
- **Why:** the guide says it saves context tokens because agents already know how to reach every feature.
- The talk describes cloud agents reproducing bugs from reports. I found no written spec for tracing a screenshot back to a screen.

**2. CLIs bundled in skills**
- The generated verify skill has fixed sections: Launch (with readiness check and teardown), Doctor (a read-only "is this instance worth driving?" check), Drive, Evidence, Cleanup, and Helpers.
- Helpers must be executable scripts inside the skill directory, with how to run them documented in the skill body. Any harness fix has to be re-run live before it ships.
- The reasoning is in `principle-build-the-lever`: build a deterministic script instead of doing the work by hand, because "the tool is one artifact a reviewer can read and rerun." Reruns cost nothing. Scripts delegated to other agents sit outside their editing scope so the contract stays fixed.

**3. Verification layers and order**
- The trust progression is local verification skills first (watching the agent's tool calls), then cloud agents, then automated end-to-end workflows. The talk warns against spinning up many agents before you trust one locally.
- The check depends on the change: CLI changes run the real command, UI changes walk the flow in the running app, parsers and migrations replay saved input, performance compares before/after profiles, storage reads the value back. "It compiles" doesn't count.
- On top of that sit CI structural checks: banning `useEffect`, banning comments, and dependency-graph checks that keep Electron main and renderer code apart. Multi-model review adds another layer.

**4. Comment ban enforcement**
- The talk says comments are banned and stripped because agents write irrelevant or wrong ones.
- In pstack the enforcement is a `/no-comments` skill. It spawns a "Comment Sicko" subagent that audits the diff against the base branch and deletes, redesigns or fixes the root cause. A comment that says "do not remove" survives only if it refers to a dependency that can't change. Otherwise the agent offers to enforce the rule with types, runtime checks or lint instead.
- The skill itself ships no hook or lint rule. The CI ban is in her app, not in pstack.

**5. PR output for humans**
- The rule is "small ordered commits, evidence in the description."
- `/show-me-your-work` says "Evidence is a pointer, not prose": commit SHAs, `file:line`, artifact and trace paths, screenshot baseline directories (e.g. `commit 7c21e0a, pixel-diff 0`).
- Overnight runs keep a TSV decision log with columns time | phase | decision | reason | evidence pointer | result. A reviewer on a different model family audits it.
- One contradiction with the talk's framing: the pstack guide says babysit "never merges, even with everything green." So pstack stops at merge-ready. Any auto-merge happens in her setup, not in the public plugin.

**Ranked corrections**
`principle-encode-lessons-in-structure` ranks enforcement from strongest to weakest: unrepresentable states, then lint rules or banned APIs, then canonical helpers, then runtime checks. It says "agents copy whatever the surrounding code already does" (the "code is memory" idea) and "the instruction is the symptom." Prose like a style guide falls below all four.

## My inference (not sourced)
- I found no written source for the phrases "code is memory", "engineers as gardeners", or "style guides least trusted". They are probably only in the video. The structure ranking above is the closest written version.
- The feature map is most likely used for bug reproduction like this: match the screenshot's screen to a feature file, follow its access steps with the CDP harness, then collect evidence using the skill's Evidence standard.
- This closely matches our `.claude/rules` and CDP-driving memories. Copying the Launch/Doctor/Drive/Evidence/Cleanup skill template plus a `features/` map looks like a direct win for Obsidian and Roam verification.

|---|---|
| Fixing the PR body style | `create-pr` writes Review focus / Decisions / Verification / Known limits. The repo template requires Reviewer brief / Loom / Scope check / Delegated review. The skill and the template disagree, so every body needs fixing. |
| Checking tests and verification | `create-pr` runs per-app `check-types` and `lint`. AGENTS.md requires `pnpm ci:validate` from the root, so CI catches what the skill skipped. |
| Bot round-trips | babysit knows about Bugbot, but the sweep script's bot list doesn't include Bugbot or Cursor, so their comments aren't picked up. |
| Running reviews one by one | You have six overlapping review paths. review-like-michael is a subset of pre-pr-review and is older. |
| Checking behaviour | The Obsidian CDP verify skill only exists in a worktree (`obsidian-cdp-verify-skill`). It's never been merged to main, and it sits in a folder the skill loader doesn't read. |

Fixing these five would remove most of the manual steps with no new ideas at all. I'd do this first.

## Where the trust gaps are

Here is where I think trust currently breaks, most important first:

1. **"Did it actually work?"** Evidence from running the app. This is the big one. Right now the proof is "types pass" plus a Loom you record yourself.
2. **"Did it do only what was asked?"** scope-check already covers this.
3. **"Is it consistent with the codebase?"** pre-pr-review and the delegated review cover this.
4. **"Did it hide a problem?"** Workaround comments, `as` casts, handling one edge case instead of fixing the cause. This is where her comment ban comes in.
5. **"Can I check it quickly?"** The output has to be skimmable at human speed. Evidence should be pointers (screenshot, command, file:line), not prose.

Items 2 and 3 are in good shape. Items 1, 4 and 5 are where the gains are.

## Your questions about the talk

The talk is backed by an open plugin called **pstack** (github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack). Its skills are plain markdown, so they work outside Cursor.

**Why keep a CLI in the skill directory instead of letting the agent write scripts?** The agent still writes the check for each change. What it stops rewriting is the harness: launching the app, attaching, waiting until it's ready, taking screenshots, tearing down. That's where the flakiness lives. A harness rewritten every session breaks in a new way every time, and you can't trust evidence from a harness nobody reviewed. Your own memories show this. "Contested vault plugin dir, grep the bundle", "tldraw store.put doesn't autosave" and "Escape needs a keymap scope" are all harness problems that belong in a script's pre-flight check, not in memory notes. You already do this well for Roam: the Playwright `loadExtension` script with ready/run/cleanup hooks is exactly this pattern. Obsidian just needs the same thing.

pstack's verify skill always has the same sections: **Launch, Doctor, Drive, Evidence, Cleanup**. Doctor is a read-only check that answers "is this instance worth driving?" In our case that means catching problems like the wrong plugin build in the vault.

**What a feature map looks like in practice.** It's plain markdown, not generated code:

```
.agents/skills/verify-obsidian/features/
  README.md              ← index of the top 3–5 features
  node-creation.md       ← 4 sections: sub-features / how a user reaches it
  relations-panel.md       (command id, ribbon, hotkey) / how the harness
  canvas.md                drives it (selectors, executeCommandById) / gotchas
```

A daily job checks two things. One is the source code, looking for drift. The other is a live walk through every feature. Each mismatch is sorted as either "the map is out of date" or "the product has a regression".

When a bug report arrives as a screenshot and "???", the agent matches the screen to a feature file, follows its access steps with the harness, and reproduces the bug.

It isn't an argument for backfilling tests. It's a navigation guide that makes checks cheap to write. Start with 3–5 features, not full coverage.

**Comments.** pstack ranks how rules get enforced, strongest first: states the types can't represent, then lint or banned APIs, then shared helpers, then runtime checks. Written prose like a style guide comes last. Your create-pr step trims comments to one line. Her version asks a different question: is this comment covering a workaround? If yes, fix the cause or delete it. I'd change the audit to ask that question rather than add an outright ban. A ban conflicts with STYLE_GUIDE.md, so it's a team decision to raise with Michael.

## A proposed flow

```
YOU  /start → plan together (grilling, prototype, diagrams) → approve plan   ◀ gate 1
     └─ plan diagram saved to the checkpoint _context.md
AGENT implement ⇄ verify-<app> (Doctor → Drive via feature map → Evidence)
      → /create-pr: ci:validate · pre-pr-review · delegated review · scope-check
        body = template headings + plan diagram + evidence table (screenshots)
      → draft PR → babysit loop (CI + all bots incl. Bugbot) until green
YOU  read evidence + diff, record Loom, mark ready                            ◀ gate 2
```

- **Planning stays fully yours.** Two installed skills you don't seem to use would help there. `mattpocock-skills:grilling` stress-tests a plan. `mattpocock-skills:prototype` answers a design question with throwaway code.
- **Diagram reuse** fits in naturally. The Mermaid diagram from planning gets saved in the checkpoint, and `create-pr` puts it into the Reviewer brief, so the PR shows the architecture you agreed on.
- **The Loom** is the biggest recurring human cost. Once an evidence table with screenshots exists, it may be worth asking the team whether it can replace the Loom for small PRs.

## Suggested order

1. **Fix the gaps above (hours):** align the create-pr body with the template, switch to `ci:validate`, add Bugbot to the sweep list, remove the reference to `/demo-handoff` (it doesn't exist), and retire review-like-michael.
2. **Merge the Obsidian CDP skill** into `.agents/skills`, restructured into Launch/Doctor/Drive/Evidence/Cleanup, and add an Obsidian entry to `launch.json`.
3. **Write feature maps for 3 Obsidian features.**
4. **Put the evidence table and plan diagram in the PR body.**
5. **Change the comment audit to "workaround → fix the cause"**, and move repeat offenders into lint rules. Reviewdog makes new lint rules cheap.

## To decide the next step

- Which of the five trust gaps hurts you most in practice? I'm guessing #1, but you have the review history.
- Should step 1 start now? It's small. I'd plan it and then edit the skills.
- Is the Loom rule open for discussion with the team?

input.prompt:
Read-only analysis in repo /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph (origin/main is fetched; use `git show origin/main:<path>` / `gh pr view/diff` — do not checkout or edit anything).

Primary: PR #1463 "ENG-2254 Set up testing infrastructure for Obsidian" (merged, commit ec000758e by maparent). Get `gh pr view 1463 --comments` and `gh pr diff 1463`. Report:
1. Exactly what it sets up: vitest config (environment? jsdom/node?), how the `obsidian` module is mocked/stubbed (the npm `obsidian` package has no runtime), any fixtures/test helpers/fake App/Vault/MetadataCache, example tests written, CI wiring (does root ci:validate / test:unit now include obsidian?), any README/AGENTS.md docs or conventions it establishes (file naming, colocated vs __tests__).
2. What kinds of code it can test well (pure utils, frontmatter/yaml, relations.json logic, import/export converters) vs can't (React UI, CM6, tldraw, real Obsidian APIs).
3. Review discussion: any stated intent/follow-ups, reviewer requests, deferred scope, linked Linear ticket intent.
4. Current usage on main: count of *.test.ts files under apps/obsidian on origin/main and which areas they cover; any later PRs that added tests.

Secondary (brief, ~1 paragraph each):
- PR #1412 (open, sid597) "Add Roam and Obsidian round-trip tests": what harness it uses, does it build on #1463.
- PR #1327 (open, trangdoan982) "Add dg-obsidian-cdp-verify skill": what scripts it bundles, state, review comments.
- PR #959 (open) "ENG-1583 Automate Obsidian dev environment e2e testing": Playwright/Electron approach, state, why stalled (comments).
- PR #1371 (merged) "ENG-2212 Port cross-platform Roam Playwright workflows": the pattern of scripts + test-module hooks — useful as a model for Obsidian.

Then give your assessment: how these layers (unit vitest / round-trip / CDP live-drive / Playwright e2e) fit together as a verification ladder, overlaps, and what's the minimal path to an agent being able to self-verify Obsidian changes at each layer. Include file paths and concrete snippets of key helper APIs (short). Under 1200 words.

content.text:
## What PR #1463 set up

It gives Obsidian vitest unit tests in plain Node, with a hand-written `obsidian` stub at `apps/obsidian/test/obsidianStub.ts`. Obsidian's npm package has no runtime, so the stub stands in for the members code actually uses, and `check-types` fails if the stub drifts from the real Obsidian types. It's already part of `ci:validate`, and `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md` documents the conventions. Four test files use it so far. There's no fake App or Vault; the convention is to build just the slice the code reads and cast it with `as unknown as App`.

It can test pure logic: utils, frontmatter, paths, `relations.json`, converters. It can't test React, CodeMirror, tldraw, modals or real vault events.

This is the bottom rung of the ladder. The upper rungs are all open PRs, and some of them overlap:

| Layer | What it proves | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Unit tests (#1463) | Logic is correct | ✅ on main |
| 2. Round-trip across apps (#1412, Sid) | Roam ⇄ Obsidian converters agree | Draft. **It doesn't build on #1463**: it brings its own Obsidian mock and will clash with the stub when rebased onto main. |
| 3. CDP driving the running app (#1327, yours) | Real Obsidian behaves correctly | Draft, no human review. Devin found a wrong plugin folder name in the pre-flight check. Its note "no test runner" is now out of date. |
| 4. Playwright e2e (#959, yours) | Same, but it launches Obsidian with a throwaway vault, so it can run unattended | Stalled since June. Its helpers duplicate most of #1327. |

The merged Roam Playwright port, **#1371**, is the model to copy. One command owns build, load, readiness and proof, and the caller supplies only `ready` / `run` / `cleanup` hooks. That's the same Launch/Doctor/Drive/Evidence/Cleanup structure as pstack.

**How this plugs into the workflow:** the agent chooses the lowest rung that can prove the change. Logic changes get a unit test, which is then permanent regression cover. UI changes get a hook module run through the loader, which captures screenshots into the evidence table. Over time the per-feature hook modules add up to the feature map: each `features/<x>.md` points at the hook that drives that feature.

Some choices here affect the whole team, so I have a few questions before recommending further:

questions.question: When an agent's PR loses your trust, what's usually the cause? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Works on paper, broken in app
options.description: Types and CI are green, but the behaviour is wrong or a regression shows up only when you click through it.

options.label: Reviewers catch what I missed
options.description: Bots or Michael find bugs, pattern violations or reuse misses after the PR is up, which means more rounds.

options.label: Over-built or off-scope
options.description: Extra abstractions, one-off edge-case handling, workaround comments, or changes beyond the ticket.

options.label: Can't tell what it did
options.description: The diff is hard to audit quickly. You're unsure what was verified and how, or why a decision was made.

questions.question: For live Obsidian verification (layers 3–4), which path should we take?

options.label: Merge #1327, fold #959 in later (Recommended)
options.description: Fix and merge the CDP skill now (it attaches to your open vault) so agents can self-verify this week. Later, turn it into a #1371-style loader script with a throwaway-vault mode taken from #959.

options.label: Build the full loader now
options.description: Go straight to one `obsidian:verify --test-module` command that combines #1327 and #959. Cleaner, but takes longer before agents can verify anything.

options.label: Evaluate the library first
options.description: Evaluate mnaoumov/obsidian-integration-testing (which Michael pointed to) before investing in our own harness.

questions.question: Should these workflow changes be personal tooling or team conventions?

options.label: Personal first, then propose
options.description: Change your ~/.claude skills (create-pr, babysit, start) now. Only move repo-level things like the verify skill, feature maps and the PR template into the repo after they've proven themselves on a few PRs.

options.label: Team from the start
options.description: Put everything in .agents/skills and the repo, and write it up for Michael and the team now.

options.label: Split by type
options.description: Test harnesses and verify skills are team changes; PR-flow automation (create-pr, babysit, sweep) stays personal.

questions.question: Where should verification evidence go, and what about the Loom?

options.label: Evidence table in PR body, keep Loom
options.description: Screenshots plus a list of commands run and paths tested go in the Verification section. The Loom stays required. The least disruptive option.

options.label: Evidence table, propose Loom opt-out
options.description: Same table, plus propose that small PRs with screenshot evidence can skip the Loom.

options.label: Linked evidence page
options.description: The PR body links to a richer report (an HTML artifact with a diagram, screenshots and the scenario matrix). The body itself stays short.

Evaluate the GitHub library mnaoumov/obsidian-integration-testing (web research via WebFetch/WebSearch/gh api; read-only; you may read local repo /Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph for comparison but do not edit or checkout anything).

Context: Discourse Graphs Obsidian plugin (apps/obsidian) wants agent-driven live verification. Existing options:
- PR #1463 (merged): vitest unit tests with hand-written obsidian stub (apps/obsidian/test/obsidianStub.ts).
- PR #1327 (open, `gh pr diff 1327`): raw CDP driver attaching to an already-open vault on port 9222 (driver.mjs connect/evaluate/waitFor/key/typeText/reloadPlugin; harness.mjs runVerification with scenarios).
- PR #959 (open, `gh pr diff 1463` no — use `gh pr diff 959`): Playwright connectOverCDP launching Obsidian with throwaway vault; electron.launch fails on macOS since binary forks.
- PR #1371 (merged): Roam model — one command `playwright:load-extension --test-module x.mjs` with ready/run/cleanup hooks and proof capture.

Determine for the library: what it actually does (runs tests inside real Obsidian? launches Obsidian? headless? how does test code reach `app`?), install/deps, maturity (stars, last commit, releases, issues, author's other obsidian tooling like obsidian-dev-utils), license, macOS + CI (Linux/xvfb) support, whether it supports UI interaction/screenshots or only API-level tests, compatibility with vitest, and how it would handle plugin build loading. Check its README, source structure, examples, and any consumers (gh search code / dependents).

Deliver: a comparison table (library vs #1327 vs #959) on: what it proves, setup cost, agent-friendliness (can an agent run it unattended and get evidence/screenshots?), CI-ability, parallel-worktree safety, maintenance risk. Then a recommendation: adopt / adopt-partly (which parts) / skip, and a minimal spike plan (1–2 steps) to validate it on one real feature. Under 800 words, cite URLs, separate sourced facts from inference.

options.label: Decision taken

Option A: stub in-tree   ✗ drift risk
Option B: vi.mock only   ✗ no reuse
Option C: stub + conformance types  ✓ chosen
  └─ why: check-types catches drift

questions.question: Where does the diagram come from?

options.label: Plan diagram, updated at PR (Recommended)
options.description: The diagram you approve during planning is saved to the checkpoint. At PR time the agent redraws it against the actual diff and flags anything that drifted from the plan. It doubles as the over-built/off-scope check.

options.label: Generated from diff at PR time
options.description: Drawn fresh from the final diff only. Simpler, but loses the link to the decision you made.

options.label: Both, separately
options.description: The planning 'decision taken' diagram plus a separate generated map of where the diff sits.

questions.question: What format constraints matter? GitHub renders Mermaid inline, but the gh CLI can't upload images to a PR body. Screenshots need hosting somewhere.

options.label: Mermaid inline + screenshots in a comment
options.description: The diagram is Mermaid in the body. For screenshots, the agent prepares them locally and you drag them into the PR by hand (one manual step).

options.label: Mermaid inline + linked artifact
options.description: The diagram is inline. Screenshots and the scenario matrix go on a linked private artifact page. Fully automated, but reviewers click through.

options.label: Commit screenshots to a proof branch

questions.question: What should the evidence section list for each claim?

options.label: Scenario matrix
options.description: A table with one row per path or edge case the agent exercised: input, expected result, actual result, pass or fail.

options.label: Screenshots per state
options.description: Before and after, or one per key UI state, captured by the harness.

options.label: Tests added
options.description: Which new unit or round-trip tests pin the behaviour, and the command to rerun them.

content.text:
Good news on hosting: the discourse-graph MCP has `file_upload`, which puts a file in Roam and **returns the Firebase URL directly**. No block is needed, so your idea works with one tool call per screenshot. One caveat: the tool mentions decryption for encrypted graphs. If the target graph is encrypted, those URLs won't be publicly viewable, so we'd need an unencrypted graph. I haven't uploaded anything.

## Library evaluation (mnaoumov/obsidian-integration-testing)

My recommendation is to adopt it partly. It fixes the two real weaknesses in our own harnesses:
- **It launches its own Obsidian** with a temporary profile on a free port. It never touches your open vault, and parallel worktrees stop colliding. That's the contested-plugin-folder problem from your memory notes.
- **It sends trusted input and captures screenshots.** Its docs note that dispatched DOM events do nothing in CodeMirror, which is one of your CDP gotchas.
- It has a CI path under xvfb on Linux.

The risks:
- It's maintained by one person, has 3 stars, and went through **16 major versions in 6 months**, so we'd pin an exact version.
- It expects the build in `dist/dev` or `dist/build`; ours is a flat `dist/`, so we'd need a small shim.
- It needs `obsidian ^1.12.3`; we're on `^1.7.2`.
- `sharp` would be a new native dependency.

The suggested spike is one script. It would take the library's launcher and input helpers and re-run #1327's `insert-link-at-cursor` scenario, first on your Mac with your own Obsidian open, then in two worktrees at once. If that works, try it on Ubuntu with xvfb. #959 would probably be closed, and #1327's scenario style kept as the thin layer on top.

## Diagram spec, written up from your answers

**Audience:** a reviewer who just switched context. In 30 seconds they should know what the change is, what the main technical approach is, and where it sits in the feature. It's one diagram at the highest useful level, not a list of every decision.

| PR intent | Diagram shape |
|---|---|
| Bug fix | Before → after on the failing path, e.g. render steps with the broken step marked, and how the fix changes it |
| Feature | The feature's logic as a flow, with file or function names on the nodes and pseudo-code where it helps. The changed part is highlighted inside the wider feature. |
| Async, events or sync work | Runtime sequence |
| Refactor or infra | Module map before → after, plus the one decision that shaped it |

The plan diagram is reused only if it already fits one of these shapes. Otherwise it's drawn fresh from the diff.

**Evidence section:** a scenario matrix (input, expected, actual, pass or fail), screenshots for each state (Firebase URLs), tests added with the command to rerun them, and a **Not verified** list.

2. Write one script that launches its own hidden Obsidian with a temporary vault, loads our built plugin, types into the editor to run the scenario from your ENG-2114 PR (insert link at cursor), and saves a screenshot.

We'd learn in about an hour whether it launches on macOS, whether our `dist/` layout causes trouble, and whether it's reliable. Nothing gets committed. If it works, it becomes the engine behind `verify-obsidian`. If not, we fall back to finishing your CDP skill (#1327).

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

Round 1. These are the decisions that don't depend on the facts the agent is still looking up.

❓ **Q1: Screenshot page structure.** You said one page, `Trang test/`, with a block per branch and screenshots as children. A branch usually gets verified more than once (after fixes, after babysit rounds). Options:
- (a) Branch block → screenshots directly under it, with new runs appended.
- (b) Branch block → run block (`2026-09-23 · abc1234 · verify-obsidian`) → screenshot blocks, each captioned with its scenario name.
- (c) Branch block → one block per scenario → screenshots from each run under it.

➡️ **(b).** The run block ties every screenshot to a commit, so a reviewer can tell whether a screenshot predates the latest push. The PR body always links to the latest run.

---

❓ **Q2: Where the approved plan lives.** The drift check and diagram reuse at PR time both need to find the plan you approved. Options:
- (a) A section in the checkpoint `_context.md` in your Obsidian vault.
- (b) A gitignored `PLAN.md` in the worktree.
- (c) A comment on the Linear ticket.

➡️ **(a).** Checkpoint already resumes across sessions and is keyed to the worktree. I'd add an "Approved plan" section with the diagram and the file-level intent, written at gate 1. (c) makes the plan public to the team, which works against personal-first.

---

❓ **Q3: What drift does.** At PR time the agent compares the diff to the approved plan. When they differ:
- (a) Always pause and ask.
- (b) Never pause. List the drift in the PR body's "Scope beyond Done When" line.
- (c) Pause only for **unplanned structure**: new files, new abstractions or exports, or touching another app or package. Smaller drift is listed in the body.

➡️ **(c).** Structural drift is the "over-built" trust gap, so it deserves a gate. Renamed variables don't.

---

❓ **Q4: Who triggers `/create-pr`.** Gate 2 means the agent opens the draft PR. But when does it start?
- (a) You still type `/create-pr` when you feel it's done.
- (b) At gate 1 you say "ship when verified", and the agent runs create-pr itself once verification passes.
- (c) It always runs automatically after verification.

➡️ **(b), off by default.** Some tickets you'll want to poke at before a PR exists. Opting in per ticket keeps that possible.

---

❓ **Q5: Which reviews create-pr runs.** Today it runs pre-pr-review, the delegated full review and scope-check. There's also review-like-michael (from February, largely covered by pre-pr-review), the built-in `/code-review` and mattpocock's code-review.
- (a) Keep all three current reviews and drop review-like-michael.
- (b) Keep only the delegated review and scope-check, since pre-pr-review is heavy.
- (c) Add more reviewers.

➡️ **(a).** They catch different things: pre-pr-review is a mechanical checklist and predicts what reviewers will say, the delegated review is a fresh-context bug hunt, and scope-check covers scope. The "reviewers catch what I missed" loop (Q6) is the real way to raise quality. Adding reviewers isn't.

---

❓ **Q6: Where approved lessons go.** When babysit proposes turning a reviewer finding into a structural rule and you approve it, what gets written?
- (a) Always personal: memory or CLAUDE.md.
- (b) Sort by strength. A **type, lint rule, test or shared helper** goes into the current PR if it's small and in scope; otherwise it becomes a draft Linear ticket. **Prose** goes to memory or CLAUDE.md, marked "candidate for team".
- (c) Log only and review later.

➡️ **(b).** Structural fixes are the most useful form of lesson, but pulling a lint rule into an unrelated PR is scope creep, hence the ticket fallback.

---

❓ **Q7: Comment policy in create-pr.** Phase 1 currently trims comments to one line. Should it instead ask of each added comment: "does this explain a workaround?" If yes, fix the cause or delete it. If no, keep it only if it states a constraint, in two lines at most.

➡️ **Yes.** It matches your global CLAUDE.md and pstack's reasoning, and doesn't need a team-wide ban.

---

❓ **Q8: Roam in version 1?** Roam already has a working live harness (`load-extension --test-module`, which writes proof screenshots). Obsidian depends on the spike.
- (a) Obsidian only.
- (b) Both. Roam's evidence flow works on day one, and Obsidian's plugs in after the spike.

➡️ **(b).** Roam proves the evidence pipeline (capture, upload to `Trang test/`, table in the body) while the Obsidian engine is still undecided.

---

❓ **Q9: Spike pass/fail bar.** Proposed criteria:
1. It launches on macOS while your own Obsidian is open, and your Obsidian is left untouched.
2. Two worktrees can run at the same time without colliding.
3. It runs the insert-link scenario with trusted typing and captures a screenshot.
4. It takes under about 2 minutes per run.

If it fails, the fallback is to finish #1327, adding a per-worktree port and fixing the pre-flight folder name.

➡️ **Accept these criteria.** One more: Ubuntu/xvfb (CI) is a *nice-to-have*, not required for the spike, since personal-first doesn't need CI.

---

❓ **Q10: Loom.** It stays manual, and create-pr already writes a shot list. Should the shot list follow the scenario matrix, so the Loom walks through the same scenarios the agent verified?

➡️ **Yes.** The video then confirms the evidence rather than duplicating effort.

Settled so far:
- **Q5 is (b):** create-pr runs only the delegated review and scope-check.
- **Q2:** an "Approved plan" section goes into the checkpoint template.
- **Bots:** Devin, Codex and Graphite.
- **Everything else** as recommended.

On your Playwright question: yes, that works and is simpler than the MCP. `apps/roam/src/utils/mirrorAssetToRoamStorage.ts` already calls `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload`, which returns a block string with the Firebase URL. The same code also documents the forms that string can take. So inside an authenticated Playwright page, the flow is:
1. Turn the PNG bytes into a `File`.
2. Call `file.upload`.
3. Parse the URL out of the result.
4. Create the blocks with `roamAlphaAPI.data.block.create`.

No MCP setup is needed. I'm dropping the MCP approach.

On the Q9 vault check: `apps/obsidian/.env` only sets `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH`, which is where the dev build gets copied into your vault. That raises a new question about which vault verification uses, so Round 2 starts there.

---

❓ **Q11: Which vault Obsidian verification uses.** The library normally launches its own Obsidian with a **temporary vault**, which can't collide with anything. Your check only matters when testing against the **vault in `.env`**. Options:
- (a) Always a temporary vault seeded with a small set of fixture files. Needs no collision check, but the fixture has to be maintained.
- (b) Always the `.env` vault: realistic data and your real settings. The Doctor step first finds that vault from `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH` and checks whether a running Obsidian with a debug port already has it open. If one does, it stops and tells you to point `.env` at another vault.
- (c) Temporary by default, with `--vault env` switching to (b) and its check.

➡️ **(c).** Most scenarios need only a few notes, and a temporary vault makes parallel worktrees safe. For bugs that need real data, `--vault env` plus your check applies. The spike tests both modes.

---

❓ **Q12: Which Playwright slot does uploading.** The upload needs an authenticated Roam session on `discourse-dev-graph`. Slot profiles are locked while in use, so if slot 1 is busy with a test, an upload on slot 1 fails. Options:
- (a) Reuse whichever slot the verification ran in, and upload before closing it.
- (b) Keep one slot (say slot 3) just for uploads.
- (c) Try slot 1, and fall back to the next free slot.

➡️ **(a) for Roam PRs, since the session is already open, and (c) for Obsidian PRs.** No slot sits reserved and idle. This assumes every slot in your `.env` points at `discourse-dev-graph`. Tell me if slots 2 and 3 point elsewhere.

---

❓ **Q13: Where the upload tool lives.** It has to import the repo's `roamSession.ts` helpers, but you chose personal tooling first. Options:
- (a) A personal script in `~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/`, run with `tsx` from the current worktree and importing the repo's session module.
- (b) A new repo script (`pnpm --filter roam playwright:upload-evidence`), which is a team change.
- (c) Put the logic in a Playwright `--test-module` hook, so the existing `load-extension` command does the upload.

➡️ **(a).** It keeps the change personal, and the script is small: take a folder of PNGs, a branch name and a run label, and return a list of URLs. If it holds up over a few PRs, propose it as (b). (c) ties uploading to Roam PRs only.

---

❓ **Q14: What to keep from pre-pr-review.** Dropping it loses two cheap checks: the diff-size gate (warn over roughly 500 lines, which is Michael's preference) and "every bot comment resolved". Options:
- (a) Drop both.
- (b) Put both into create-pr Phase 2 as one-line checks.
- (c) Keep only the diff-size warning.

➡️ **(b).** Both are cheap and each has cost a review round before. pre-pr-review's longer passes (data invariants, predicted reviewer comments) stay available when you ask for them.

---

❓ **Q15: Unknown bots.** The sweep currently drops silently any `[bot]` login not on its list. Should it report them as `bot:<login>` instead, so a newly added reviewer bot isn't missed?

➡️ **Yes.** Deploy bots like Vercel, Supabase and Linear go on an ignore list instead.

---

❓ **Q16: How to roll out and measure it.** Proposed order:
1. Plumbing: create-pr body, `ci:validate`, the comment audit, bot sweep, babysit step 4, the checkpoint plan section.
2. The upload script, proven on one Roam run.
3. The Obsidian spike.
4. A `verify-obsidian` skill built on whichever engine the spike picks.

Then run the next 2–3 tickets through it and record in each checkpoint **how many times you had to step in, and why**.

➡️ **Accept.** Counting interventions is the measurable form of "more autonomy at the same trust", and it tells us which rung to improve next.

- (a) **Copy the slot vault into a temporary folder for each run** and launch against the copy. Your fixtures never change and runs can happen in parallel. Your "vault already open?" check only matters in (b).
- (b) **Open in place:** the run changes the real vault. The Doctor step checks whether any Obsidian with a debug port has that vault open. If one does, it stops and tells you to switch.

Q18: yes, or simply an array of paths, since Obsidian doesn't require login

**Q17:** Mostly yes. An Obsidian vault carries its own setup in the `.obsidian/` folder: installed plugins (their code, not just a list), which ones are enabled, and their settings, hotkeys, themes and workspace layout. Copying the folder copies all of that. The differences:

| Difference | Handling |
|---|---|
| Our DG plugin in the copy | Replaced with the current worktree's build. That's what we want to test. |
| Sync plugins (Obsidian Sync, obsidian-git, Remotely Save…) in the copy | **Real risk:** they could push the test run's edits back to your real remote. The copy disables them before launch, and the Doctor step lists any it finds. |
| Obsidian asks whether to trust a new vault's plugins on first open | The launcher has to get past that prompt. The spike checks this. |
| Dataview/Datacore indexes | Rebuilt on first open. The first run is slower, but the results are the same. |
| Plugin folders that are symlinks (like the dev mirror) | The copy follows the links, so it doesn't share them with the real vault. |

So copy by default, with in-place mode as a fallback. For your deletion rule: cleanup only ever removes the temporary copy, and it refuses any path outside the scratch folder. In-place runs never delete files or folders.

**Q18:** Settled as one list: `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS=/path/a,/path/b` in `apps/obsidian/.env`, with `--slot N` picking a vault by position.

## Everything we decided

**Gates**
1. Planning stays yours.
2. At gate 1 the plan and a diagram are written to a new "Approved plan" section in checkpoint.
3. The agent opens the draft PR on its own only if you said "ship when verified" at gate 1.
4. You record the Loom (its shot list follows the scenario matrix) and mark the PR ready.

**create-pr**
- **Reviews:** the delegated review and scope-check only. pre-pr-review is dropped.
- **Checks:** `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm ci:validate`, plus two one-line checks: diff size over ~500 lines, and all bot comments resolved.
- **Comment audit:** a comment that explains a workaround means fix the cause or delete it. Other comments stay only if they state a constraint, in two lines at most.
- **Drift check** against the approved plan: it pauses only for unplanned structure (new files, new abstractions or exports, touching another app or package). Smaller drift is listed in the body.
- **Body:** the PR template's headings. It carries one reviewer diagram, shaped by what the PR does. The plan diagram is reused only if it fits.
- **Evidence section:** scenario matrix, screenshots for each state, tests added with the command to rerun them, and a "Not verified" list.

**babysit and the sweep**
- The sweep covers Devin, Codex and Graphite, reports unknown `[bot]` logins, and ignores deploy bots.
- babysit gets a step 4: after fixing a finding, it proposes the strongest way to encode the lesson and waits for your yes.
  - A type, lint rule, test or helper goes into the current PR if it's small and in scope. Otherwise it becomes a draft ticket.
  - Prose goes to memory or CLAUDE.md, marked as a candidate for the team.

**Evidence hosting**
- A personal `~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence` script.
- It uses a Playwright session and `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` to put screenshots on the `Trang test/` page in `discourse-dev-graph`, nested as branch → run (date · commit · harness) → screenshot blocks.
- Roam PRs use the slot the verification already opened. Obsidian PRs use slot 1, falling back to the next free one.

**Obsidian verification**
- A spike on `obsidian-integration-testing`.
- **Pass criteria:** it launches alongside your own Obsidian without touching it, runs in parallel worktrees, types for real and captures a screenshot, and takes under ~2 minutes. CI on Linux is a nice-to-have.
- **Vaults:** your listed vaults, copied for each run with sync plugins disabled, or used in place with the "already open?" check.
- **Fallback:** finish #1327.

**Rollout**
1. Plumbing.
2. The upload script, proven on one Roam run.
3. The spike.
4. The `verify-obsidian` skill.
5. Pilot it on 2–3 tickets, counting in each checkpoint how often and why you had to step in.

Obsidian is Electron, so it can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Relaunch with
`open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222`, then attach over
`ws` to the target from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list`. Verified working August 2026 on
Obsidian 1.8.4 / macOS — 23/23 assertions driving the ENG-2113 search footer.

Key points learned the hard way:

- **Attach to an already-open vault** instead of rewriting `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`
  to select one. The rewrite is how PR #959 selects a vault and it is also that PR's worst bug —
  if launch throws afterwards, teardown never runs and the user's global Obsidian config stays clobbered.
- Several CDP page targets exist (devtools, popouts, one per vault). Pick by
  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- **Force the renderer active over CDP instead of fighting for window focus.** Two calls at connect
  time make occlusion throttling irrelevant:
  `Page.setWebLifecycleState {state:"active"}` and `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled {enabled:true}`.
  Without them, `osascript -e 'tell application "Obsidian" to activate'` only holds until the next
  command returns focus to the terminal, and Reading view silently renders an **empty**
  `.markdown-preview-section` — links, Properties and backlinks all absent, no error. Verified
  September 2026 on Obsidian 1.13.7: the identical scenario went from `body link rendered: false`
  to `true` with those two calls added. The note below still describes the underlying throttling.
- **The Obsidian window must be visible (`document.visibilityState === "visible"`) while scenarios
  run.** When it is covered/minimised/on another Space, Chromium throttles the renderer's timers —
  100 ms → 300–900 ms, and after ~5 min hidden to once per minute — so anything built on
  `setTimeout` (a 500 ms save debounce, a sync debounce, a poll loop *inside* the page) silently
  stalls. It presents as "the feature is broken" (writes land minutes later) with zero errors.

  believing a timing failure; `electronWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` helps only until focus changes,

- **`editor.hasFocus()` is not measurable from CDP.** It reads `false` even for a plain

  focus at all (`document.activeElement` is the top-level app div). Take a **baseline** measurement
  of the same assertion outside the feature under test before believing a focus failure — ENG-2114
  looked like a focus regression until the baseline failed identically. Assert the observable
  consequence instead (cursor position advanced past the inserted text).
- **Stale `.modal-container` elements poison selectors.** A scenario that times out or throws leaves
  its modal in the DOM, so the next run's `querySelector(".modal-container .modal")` reads the *old*

  actually works. Start every scenario with

- The plugin **folder** is `discourse-graphs` but the **id** is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; passing the

  `a.internal-link` therefore cannot leak into either, whatever it scans. Both panels are also

  type: reference
---

Every worktree's `apps/obsidian` dev watcher mirrors to the **same** vault plugin directory
(`<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs`). With watchers running in several worktrees, one
of them rebuilding replaces your `main.js` at any moment — including *between* two CDP
verification runs.

Observed on ENG-2231: verification passed, then the next run reported zero decorations and a
missing injected `<style>`. Cause was not the code — a watcher in
`eng-1249-...-overlay-feature` had re-mirrored its own build, and the vault's `main.js` again
contained `TagNodeHandler`, the class the change had just deleted.

**Check before believing any live result:**

```bash
V=<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/discourse-graphs
ps aux | grep "[s]cripts/dev.ts"          # who else is watching
grep -c "<symbol you just added>" $V/main.js
grep -c "<symbol you just deleted>" $V/main.js   # must be 0
```

Prefer a one-shot `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<vault path> npx tsx scripts/build.ts` chained in the
**same command** as the verification, rather than a long-lived watcher, so the window for another
watcher to clobber it is as small as possible.

Related: [[reference-obsidian-shared-plugin-mirror]], [[reference-obsidian-cdp-driving]].

## Our CDP driver vs obsidian-integration-testing

Both drive Obsidian over CDP. The real difference is **whose Obsidian they drive**.

| | Our CDP driver (#1327 plus your memory notes) | obsidian-integration-testing |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | Raw CDP over `ws`, about 150 lines, no dependencies | CDP through puppeteer-core and webdriverio |
| Which Obsidian | **Yours.** It attaches to your open app on port 9222. | **A separate instance** with its own temporary profile (`--user-data-dir`) and its own port |
| Single-instance problem | You must have started Obsidian with the port. Otherwise you have to restart it. | Avoided. The single-instance lock belongs to a profile, so a second profile runs next to yours. |
| Vault | In place, on your chosen test vault | A temporary copy, created fresh each run |
| Your clicks during a run | **They interfere.** Your memory notes record a confident wrong diagnosis caused by exactly this. | Isolated in its own window |
| Background throttling | Solved and written down (`setWebLifecycleState` plus focus emulation) | Unknown. It hides the window off-screen, which may hit the same throttling. |
| Input | CDP `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`, which counts as real input. It worked for ENG-2114. | Electron `sendInputEvent`. Roughly equivalent. |
| Screenshots | `Page.captureScreenshot` | `captureObsidianScreenshot` |
| Parallel runs | One port. Different vaults can share the one app, since targets are picked by vault name. | Safe, one instance per run |
| Trust | **Proven by you**, for example 23/23 assertions on ENG-2113 | Not vetted: 3 stars, 16 major versions in 6 months |

One idea is worth borrowing without the library. Its isolation comes down to launching Obsidian with `--user-data-dir=<temp>` and a free port. Our driver could do the same in a few lines. That would end the "restart your Obsidian" problem and your clicks interfering, and still work in place on your test vault. The catch: a fresh profile has no vault list, so the driver writes a small `obsidian.json` *inside the temporary profile*. That's safe, unlike #959's rewrite of your global config. I'd make it an option, not the default, for now.

## Q22: CDP is "in memory" today

That's accurate. When you say "verify with CDP and screenshots", the agent reads `reference_obsidian_cdp_driving.md` (about 60 lines of gotchas) and **writes a fresh driver in its scratchpad every session**. It works, but it's exactly the pattern the talk warns about:
- Each session's driver is new code nobody reviewed, with new bugs. Evidence from it is only as good as that session's harness.
- Every hard-won lesson (throttling, stale modals, plugin id vs folder name, `iterateRootLeaves`) is prose the agent has to read and apply correctly each time. The memory note keeps growing, and nothing checks that the lessons were followed.
- The harness costs tokens to rebuild before it verifies anything.

#1327 turns that note into code: `driver.mjs` (connect, `waitFor`, keys, `reloadPlugin`), `harness.mjs` (scenarios, stale-modal cleanup) and `preflight.mjs`. After that, each session writes only the **scenario**, maybe 20 lines. The gotchas are handled by code reviewed once, and the memory note shrinks to a pointer.

So the Q22 decision is only about where that code lives:

❓ **Q22 (restated)**
- (a) Finish #1327 as a team skill in `.agents/skills`.
- (b) Keep it personal in `~/.claude/skills` for now.

➡️ **(a).** Other people's sessions would stop rewriting the driver too, and it's already an open PR.

Q19–Q21 from the last round are still open. Proposed answers:
- **Q19:** the Doctor attaches, launches or tells you to restart Obsidian.
- **Q20:** each run builds, copies into the slot vault, reloads the plugin and runs the preflight check.
- **Q21:** everything a run creates goes under `_verify/<branch>/`, and nothing is deleted.

Accept those, or change any of them?

Q22: choose (b)

# Checkpoint — record session context

Persist the **reasoning layer** of this work session (goal, decisions, dead ends,
constraints, next step) to the Obsidian vault, keyed to the current worktree.
Files are plain markdown written directly — no MCP, no Obsidian required running.

## Steps

### 1. Resolve where to write
Run the helper from the current worktree:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

It prints `TICKET`, `BRANCH`, `WORKTREE`, `SESSION_DIR`, `CONTEXT_FILE`,
`LOG_FILE`, `STAMP`, `CONTEXT_EXISTS` and creates the folders. **Only write to the
`CONTEXT_FILE` and `LOG_FILE` paths it gives you** — never elsewhere in the vault.
If it errors (not a git repo / detached HEAD), tell the user and stop.

### 2. Read existing context if present
If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, read `CONTEXT_FILE` first so you UPDATE it rather than
overwrite history. Digest sections get rewritten; accreting sections get appended.

### 3. Gather the reasoning layer
Reconstruct from this session's conversation + git. If a ticket id is present and
Linear is available, you may fetch the title/URL with `mcp__linear-server__get_issue`.
Apply the **extraction rubric** below to decide what is worth recording.

### 4. Write `_context.md`
Use the template at `~/.claude/skills/checkpoint/template.md` as the structure.
- If new file: fill the template. Set `created`/`updated` to today, `sessions: 1`.
- If updating: rewrite digest sections (TL;DR, Current state, Next step, Open
  questions, key_files, status), **append** to accreting sections (Key decisions,
  Dead ends, Constraints, Gotchas) with a dated bullet, bump `updated` to today
  and increment `sessions`.

### 5. Append a log snapshot
Write a short dated entry to `LOG_FILE` (a fresh file — no append needed):
a 3–6 line summary of what THIS session accomplished + what changed since last time.
This is the immutable audit trail; `_context.md` is the living digest.

### 6. Confirm
Tell the user what you wrote (context file + log file paths) and the one-line Next step.

## Extraction rubric — what to record (keep it concise)

**The test:** record a line only if it would otherwise have to be *re-derived* or
would prevent *repeating a mistake*. Ask: *"What do I know now that I didn't at
session start, that isn't already in Linear, git, or the code?"*

**DO record (the reasoning layer — it evaporates when the session ends):**
- Scope agreement: how the ticket was interpreted, what's in/out of scope.
- Decisions: what + why + what was rejected + what would make us revisit it.
- Dead ends: what was tried that failed, and why.
- Constraints/preferences the user stated ("ship by Fri", "don't touch billing").
- Gotchas: environmental facts learned the hard way.
- Next step + open questions + current status.

**Do NOT record (noise / lives elsewhere):**
- Activity logs ("edited foo.ts, ran tests") — record outcomes, not keystrokes.
- Anything copy-pasteable from the diff, git history, or the Linear ticket body.
- Resolved questions — delete them or fold the answer into a decision.
- Restating how the code works — that's what the code is for.

**Mark uncertainty** explicitly (`*assumed*`, `*unchecked*`). Prefer 8 sharp lines
over 40 vague ones — this must stay skimmable for the user, not just parseable by an agent.

**How to apply:** when the task is not a ticket/branch-scoped coding task, create and use a descriptive session folder (e.g. `AI_sessions/OKR_meeting`) instead of the branch-derived one, while still following the checkpoint template structure (`_context.md` + dated log file) inside it.
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# session-context.sh — helper for the per-worktree session-context recorder.
#
# All session files live UNDER $SESSION_VAULT_DIR (an Obsidian vault subfolder).
# One folder per ticket/worktree, keyed by the git branch name:
#
#   $SESSION_VAULT_DIR/<branch>/
#     _context.md        <- canonical current state (the next agent reads this)
#     log/<date-time>.md <- append-only per-session checkpoint snapshots
#
# Subcommands:
#   resolve            Print KEY=VALUE lines describing where to read/write for
#                      the current git worktree. Creates the folders. Used by the
#                      /checkpoint skill and the start/go-ticket commands.
#   snapshot           SessionEnd safety net: append a compact git-state snapshot
#                      to the log IFF the worktree has real work (dirty or ahead).
#                      No LLM, deterministic, silent no-op when nothing to record.
#
# Config:
#   SESSION_VAULT_DIR  Root folder for session files.
#                      Default: /Users/trang.doan/Documents/testVault/AI_sessions
set -euo pipefail

VAULT="${SESSION_VAULT_DIR:-/Users/trang.doan/Documents/testVault/AI_sessions}"
# Branches that never get a session folder (not real work sessions).
BASE_BRANCHES_RE='^(main|master|develop|dev|release|staging)$'

die() { echo "session-context: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# Resolve the git worktree root for the current directory (empty if not a repo).
repo_root() { git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true; }

current_branch() { git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true; }

# Guardrail: ensure a path is strictly inside the vault before we touch it.
assert_in_vault() {
  local p="$1"
  case "$p" in
    "$VAULT"/*) : ;;
    *) die "refusing to write outside vault: $p (vault=$VAULT)";;
  esac
}

cmd_resolve() {
  local root branch
  root="$(repo_root)"
  [ -n "$root" ] || die "not inside a git repository"
  branch="$(current_branch)"
  [ -n "$branch" ] && [ "$branch" != "HEAD" ] || die "no named branch (detached HEAD?)"

  # Folder key = branch name, with any '/' flattened to '-' so the vault stays flat
  # (Linear branches may be prefixed, e.g. "trang/eng-1271-title").
  # Ticket = first LINEAR-style id found anywhere in the branch, else the branch.
  local key ticket
  key="${branch//\//-}"
  if [[ "$branch" =~ ([A-Za-z]+-[0-9]+) ]]; then
    ticket="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  else
    ticket="$key"
  fi

  local session_dir context_file log_file stamp
  session_dir="$VAULT/$key"
  assert_in_vault "$session_dir"
  stamp="$(date +%Y-%m-%d-%H%M)"
  context_file="$session_dir/_context.md"
  log_file="$session_dir/log/$stamp.md"

  mkdir -p "$session_dir/log"

  local exists=no
  [ -f "$context_file" ] && exists=yes

  printf 'TICKET=%s\n'        "$ticket"
  printf 'BRANCH=%s\n'        "$branch"
  printf 'WORKTREE=%s\n'      "$root"
  printf 'SESSION_DIR=%s\n'   "$session_dir"
  printf 'CONTEXT_FILE=%s\n'  "$context_file"
  printf 'LOG_FILE=%s\n'      "$log_file"
  printf 'STAMP=%s\n'         "$stamp"
---

# Plan: agentic PR workflow v1 (personal tooling)

Status: **draft, awaiting approval** · 2026-09-23 · decisions in [[_context]]

```
YOU    /start → plan together → approve  ─────────────────────────────── gate 1
         └─ /checkpoint writes "## Approved plan" (diagram, file intent, ship-when-verified y/n)
AGENT  implement ⇄ verify at the lowest rung that proves it
         vitest (+ obsidianStub) · Roam load-extension · dg-obsidian-cdp-verify
         └─ screenshots → pr-evidence → Roam "Trang test/" → Firebase URLs
       /create-pr: comment audit · ci:validate · size/bot checks · delegated review
                   · scope-check · plan-drift check · body (template + writing style
                   + reviewer diagram + evidence) · draft PR
       babysit loop (CI + Devin/Codex/Graphite) → step 4 lesson proposal → you approve
YOU    review draft, record Loom (shot list = scenario matrix), mark ready ──── gate 2
```

---

## Phase 1: Plumbing (personal skills)

### 1.1 Checkpoint: "Approved plan" section
- `~/.claude/skills/checkpoint/template.md`: add `## Approved plan` after Goal. It holds:
  - a Mermaid diagram
  - intent per file or module
  - an `ship_when_verified: yes|no` line
- Also add an accreting `## Interventions` section: dated bullets recording when the human stepped in and why (used by the Phase 4 pilot).
- `checkpoint/SKILL.md`: when the user approves a plan, write that section verbatim (it's a digest section, so it gets rewritten on re-approval).
- **Verify:** run `/checkpoint` on a scratch branch with a toy plan, then `grep -A5 "## Approved plan"` in its `_context.md`.

### 1.2 create-pr rewrite (`~/.claude/skills/create-pr/SKILL.md`)
Phases in order:

0. **Load context.** Run `session-context.sh resolve` and read the Approved plan. If there's no plan, warn and continue; the drift check is then skipped. Remove the call to pre-pr-review.
1. **Comment audit.** For each added comment: if it explains a workaround, fix the cause or delete it. Otherwise keep it only if it states a constraint, in 2 lines at most.
2. **Checks.**
   - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm ci:validate` from the worktree root.
   - Prettier check on the changed files.
   - Diff over ~500 lines: warn.
   - Unresolved bot review threads: a `gh api graphql` query on `reviewThreads.isResolved`. Block if any remain.
3. **Reviews.** `dg-delegated-full-review`, then `scope-check`. Each finding is either fixed or listed as a known limit.
4. **Drift check** against the Approved plan. Pause and ask only for unplanned structure: new files, new exports or abstractions, or touching another app or package. Anything smaller goes on the template's "Scope beyond Done When" line.
5. **Body.**
   - Read `.github/pull_request_template.md` **at runtime** (never a copy stored in the skill) and fill its headings.
   - Reviewer brief: one Mermaid diagram chosen by PR intent. Bug fix: before → after on the failing path. Feature: logic with file names and pseudo-code. Async: a sequence diagram. Refactor: a module map. Reuse the plan diagram only if it fits.
   - Verification: scenario matrix, screenshot URLs, tests added with the command to rerun them, and **Not verified**.
   - Draft the prose through `dg-engineering-writing-style`.
6. **Open.**
   - `gh pr create --draft`, run automatically only if `ship_when_verified: yes`. Otherwise stop and show the body.
   - Afterwards, keep the existing sweep ack, `bind_pr`/monitor and babysit steps.
   - The Loom shot list follows the scenario matrix.
7. Add a `--dry-run` argument that runs phases 0–5 and prints the body without pushing.

- **Verify:**
  - `/create-pr --dry-run` on an existing branch (e.g. ENG-2261's).
  - The body's `##` headings must match `grep '^##' .github/pull_request_template.md` exactly.
  - `ci:validate` shows in the transcript.
  - A deliberately added workaround comment gets flagged.
  - A new file that isn't in the plan triggers the drift pause.

### 1.3 Sweep (`~/.claude/scripts/pr-comment-sweep.sh`)
- Keep `REVIEW_BOTS` (Devin, Codex, Graphite).
- Add `IGNORE_BOTS='^(vercel|supabase|linear-code)\[bot\]$'`.
- Any other `[bot]` login gets reported as `bot:<login>` instead of dropped.
- **Verify:**
  - `bash -n` and `shellcheck`.
  - `pr-comment-sweep.sh scan` against PR #1442, which has Devin, Vercel and Linear comments: Devin reported, the other two ignored.
  - With a stub login (`foo[bot]`) fed through the matching function: reported.

### 1.4 babysit step 4 (`~/.claude/skills/babysit/SKILL.md`)
- After a finding is fixed, propose the strongest way to encode the lesson, in this order: type → lint rule → test → shared helper → prose.
  - Small and in scope: goes into this PR.
  - Otherwise: a draft Linear ticket.
  - Prose: memory or CLAUDE.md, tagged `candidate-for-team`.
- Wait for approval. Don't propose again for a lesson that's already encoded.
- **Verify:** proven in the Phase 4 pilot (it needs real findings). Until then, a dry read on PR #1327's open Devin finding should produce one concrete proposal.

---

## Phase 2: Evidence upload (`~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/`)

- `SKILL.md` plus `upload.ts`, run with `tsx` from the current worktree.
- **Command:** `upload.ts --slot N --branch <b> --label "<date · sha · harness>" <png…>` (each PNG can carry a scenario caption).
- **Session:** imports the worktree's `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` to open the authenticated slot on `discourse-dev-graph`.
  - Roam PRs: run after the verification's `load-extension` has finished, on the same slot (its profile is unlocked by then).
  - Obsidian PRs: slot 1, falling back to the next free slot.
- **Inside the page:**
  1. Find or create the page `Trang test/`, then the branch block, then a new run block.
  2. For each PNG: `File` from base64 → `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload`.
  3. Parse the URL out of the result, following the result forms already handled in `apps/roam/src/utils/mirrorAssetToRoamStorage.ts`.
  4. Create a child block with the caption and `![](url)`.
- **Output:** JSON (`runBlockUid`, `[{caption,url}]`) plus a ready-to-paste Markdown table.
- **Verify:**
  - Upload 2 PNGs under branch `pr-evidence-smoke`.
  - Read the structure back with `roamAlphaAPI.q`: page → branch → run → 2 children.
  - `curl -sI <url>` with no cookies returns `200 image/png`. This proves the URLs are public, and rules out an encrypted graph.
  - Rerun: the same branch block gets a second run block, not a duplicate branch block.

---

## Phase 3: Obsidian CDP verify skill (`~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/`)

### 3.1 Import and restructure
- Copy `driver.mjs`, `harness.mjs`, `preflight.mjs`, `websocket.mjs` and `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` from the `obsidian-cdp-verify-skill` worktree (PR #1327).
- Rewrite `SKILL.md` into the sections **Launch / Doctor / Drive / Evidence / Cleanup / Gotchas**.
- The gotchas move out of the memory note `reference_obsidian_cdp_driving.md` into the skill. The memory note shrinks to a pointer to the skill.

### 3.2 Doctor (`doctor.mjs`, read-only)
1. Read `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` from `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env` and choose the vault for `--slot N`.
2. Check the vault lock at `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (pid + branch). If a live process from another run holds it, **stop and tell the user to switch vault**. This is the Q9 check: the vault is already being driven.
3. Obsidian state (Q19):
   - Running with a debug port: attach and open the vault with `obsidian://open?path=`.
   - Running without a port: stop and tell the user to restart it with the port.
   - Not running: launch with `--remote-debugging-port`.
4. At connect: `Page.setWebLifecycleState active` and `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled`.

### 3.3 Deliver the build (Q20)
- Chain these in one command:
  - `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/<folder> npx tsx scripts/build.ts`
  - `reloadPlugin(<id from app.plugins.manifests>)`
  - the preflight marker check
- **Fix:** preflight currently checks the wrong folder name. The folder is `discourse-graphs` and the id is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; resolve both from `manifests`.

### 3.4 Run, evidence, cleanup (Q21)
- Scenario modules export `{ name, setup, run, expect }`. The harness records one row per scenario: input, expected, actual, pass/fail, and a screenshot path under `local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<run>/`.
- Notes a run creates go under `_verify/<branch>/`. Edits to existing notes are listed in the matrix.
- **Never delete folders.** Cleanup only dismisses modals, resets the workspace and releases the lock.
- Writes `last-run.json`, which feeds both pr-evidence and the create-pr scenario matrix.

- **Verify:**
  - Port the ENG-2114 insert-link scenario, then exercise every branch:
    - Obsidian not running: it launches.
    - Running with a port: it attaches.
    - Running without a port: it notifies and stops.
    - A foreign `main.js` (another worktree's build): preflight fails.
    - The lock held by a fake live pid: it notifies to switch vault.
  - End to end: the screenshots are uploaded through pr-evidence, and the matrix and URLs render in a `--dry-run` create-pr body.

---

## Phase 4: Pilot, then propose to the team
- Run the next 2–3 tickets through the whole flow and log each intervention in the checkpoint.
- **Success:**
  - The PR body needs no manual edits.
  - No manual review or validation commands get run.
  - Fewer bot rounds than the recent baseline (count them on #1442–#1444).
- **After the pilot:** propose to the team
  - updating #1327 from the personal skill
  - `pr-evidence` as a repo script
  - the reviewer diagram and evidence convention for the PR template

## Out of scope for v1
- Feature maps (they come after the verify skill exists)
- A team-wide comment ban
- Replacing the Loom
- `obsidian-integration-testing`
- CI e2e
- Rebasing #1412 onto #1463's stub (Sid's PR)

## Order and dependencies
1.1 → 1.2 (1.2 reads the plan section). 1.3 and 1.4 are independent. 2 is independent of 1. 3.4's evidence step needs 2. 4 needs all of them.

description: Review a PR or local diff for adherence to Discourse Graphs code standards and PR requirements, report concerns to the author, and return a Standards check checkbox. Use before handoff or requesting review, alongside scope-check.
---

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.
